subject: Implementation kickoff: model shortlist, context & hourly token plan
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@healthsync.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSync Ops <ops@healthsync.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Implementation kickoff: model shortlist & token profile

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for agreeing to run the onboarding for HealthSync. Per our discovery, the immediate pilot is two routes: 1) triage+summary of patient intake forms (structured templates + some free text), and 2) short clinical-code mapping (rule+LLM assist). We attached a first-pass workload sheet (healthsync_onboarding_workload_v1.xlsx) that has request counts and sample lengths. Headline numbers: average request payload ~1.8k tokens, median ~1.2k, but we anticipate many multi-page forms with bursts up to ~14k tokens. Expected early traffic: ~45k requests/day with growth to 100k/day in 6 months.

Requests: could you recommend a model shortlist for quality vs cost (server/hosted tradeoffs), and a realistic hourly token estimate (avg / 95th pct burst) for capacity planning? Also call out context-length variants we should test (4k/8k/16k). We're looking for an implementation plan we can align on for the kickoff call.

Attached: workload spreadsheet and a sample template.

Amit Shah
Head of Product, HealthSync
amit@healthsync.ai

Attachments: healthsync_onboarding_workload_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Implementation kickoff: model shortlist & token profile

Thanks Amit — got the sheet and the samples. Quick acknowledgement and some clarifying asks so we can size correctly:

- Can you confirm the % of requests that will include attachments (scanned PDFs) vs purely form text? That changes OCR + prefill token cost.
- Do you expect long conversation-style follow-up (multi-turn) in the pilot, or is it one-shot per form?
- Any SLA targets? (p95 latency below 750ms preferred for triage route).

Initial plan items we'll run on our side:
1) Run your sheet through our tokenizer + sample simulator to build per-route hourly distributions (we'll attach the parsing notes).
2) Propose model shortlist across three cost/quality tiers and recommended context-length variants (4k/8k/16k).
3) Draft autoscaling & caching policy for the Kickoff call.

Preliminary model shortlist (internal first pass):
- redwood-lynx-7b-quant-extended (cost-efficient, good for structured summaries, 8k context)
- redwood-ritchie-13b-q4 (higher quality, 8k/16k context)
- open-vicuna-33b-compat (fallback for complex clinical paraphrase where factuality matters; 16k context)

I attached a short questionnaire that will help with concurrency and batch-window assumptions. Can we schedule a 45-minute kickoff on Nov 15?

Kimberly Park
Senior CS Manager, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: onboarding_questionnaire.pdf (3 pages)

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Implementation kickoff: model shortlist & token profile

Folks — I parsed the workbook Amit sent and built an hourly profile from the sample distribution. Key numbers (rounded):

- Baseline day: 45,000 requests/day -> ~1.9M tokens/day -> ~80k tokens/hour (avg).
- Expected ramp to 100k requests/day -> ~4.2M tokens/day -> ~175k tokens/hour (avg).
- 95th percentile hourly burst (based on time-of-day clustering in the sheet): ~420k tokens/hour.
- ~22% of requests include an attached scanned doc which we expect to OCR into ~2.3k tokens extra on average.

Implications and recommendations:
1) Context sizes: run A/B on 8k default for triage summaries (covers most multi-page forms), 16k for the worst-case multi-page clinical summaries. 4k should be kept for cold-start or routing to cheaper variant for non-critical flows.
2) Model shortlist rationale:
   - redwood-lynx-7b-quant-extended (8k): cheap, good for structured extraction + summaries with reliable latency.
   - redwood-ritchie-13b-q4 (8k/16k): quality step-up; better for free-text clinical paraphrase.
   - redwood-marz-30b(16k) candidate for later if hallucination/factuality is critical (we recommend this only in dedicated mode).
3) Capacity recommendation: if 95th burst >300k tokens/hr we should assess Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) vs hosted with aggressive autoscaling. For HealthSync's projected ramp, plan for reserved burst capacity for the busier windows.
4) Ops: enable prefix/KV caching on template sections (forms start with same header blocks) — this alone can reduce token cost by ~12-18% for triage route.

Deliverables for kickoff:
- A trimmed model shortlist matrix (cost/latency/quality) + per-route context recommendations.
- A token-budget workbook with two scenarios (baseline and growth).
- Canary plan: run small percentage of traffic on each model variant for 2 weeks with quality evals.

I'll attach the token workbook export to the shared drive and draft the per-route configs.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Couple of operational notes to add:

- Autoscaling: recommend a two-tier policy — keep a baseline of hosted instances sized for avg load; allow burst via reserved pool or cross-region fallback. We'll set the threshold at ~250k tokens/hr for activating reserved burst.
- Batching window: 10–15ms continuous batching for triage route to maintain p95 latency while improving throughput.
- Fallback routing: route to 7b quant when latency budget tight or when a non-critical request is detected (we can mark routes via header).
- Pricing & procurement: given the 95th burst numbers Monica provided, I'll ask Sales Ops to prepare a dedicated burst addendum and a short-term reserved commitment plan so HealthSync doesn't get billed an excessive on-demand uplift during the ramp.

I'll add these to the kickoff agenda. Recommend we lock a date/time for Nov 15 (Kimberly suggested).

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps:

1) Models to test in the POC: redwood-lynx-7b-quant-extended (8k), redwood-ritchie-13b-q4 (8k + 16k variant), and a vicuna-compatible large model (16k) as a quality fallback. Monica will prepare the model matrix with cost/latency estimates by EOD Nov 14.
2) Token sizing: baseline ~80k tokens/hr, growth scenario ~175k tokens/hr, 95th burst ~420k tokens/hr. We will plan reserve-burst activation at 250k tokens/hr unless HealthSync prefers an alternative threshold.
3) Ops & tuning: enable prefix caching on the triage route, 10-15ms continuous batching, and model-pin rollout during the canary. Ben will coordinate with Sales Ops on a short reserved-burst contract and pricing.
4) Kickoff call: Nov 15, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite to follow). Please confirm if that window works for the HealthSync team (Amit).

- Monica: upload token workbook + per-route configs to the shared drive and link in the kickoff agenda (due Nov 14 EOD).
